description: Dependency updates arrive as PRs where CI runs BEFORE merge, instead of
resolving fresh on every run. Three CI breakages in 2026-07 came from that
gap: ruff 0.16 widened its default rule selection (#1701), the same release
began formatting Markdown (#1705), and mcp 2.0 removed mcp.server.fastmcp
(#1705, #1711). Each would have been one red PR here instead of a silent
branchPrefix MUST stay under chore/. Two repo gates depend on it: the
ci-pr-hygiene.yml's linkage check bypasses chore/* — a bot PR cannot carry a
Fixes #N. Renovate's default 'renovate/' prefix fails both gates.
separateMajorMinor/separateMultipleMajor put a major bump in its own PR.
ruff 0.16 arriving alone and red is the entire point; grouped with routine
patches it would have been merged on a green summary.

packageRules.description: CI-gating tooling: its OUTPUT decides whether the build is green, so these move deliberately and are never grouped with anything else. See the Dependency version bounds section in CLAUDE.md.

mcp is capped below 2.0 for a KNOWN incompatibility: 2.0 removed mcp.server.fastmcp, which four packages import (digigraph, digiquant, digisearch, digivault). Raising the cap requires porting to the 2.x API, so surface it on the dashboard but never open it unattended.
Runtime libraries are deliberately unbounded — an upper bound in a published library propagates to every consumer. Group their non-major updates into one reviewable PR.
GitHub Actions. Several are already SHA-pinned; Renovate keeps the trailing version comment in sync. checkout@v4 and setup-python@v5 currently emit Node 20 deprecation warnings on every run.
Security fixes jump the queue. prPriority is only valid on a packageRule, not inside vulnerabilityAlerts.
Never propose changes to the intra-monorepo path dependencies; they resolve locally, not from an index.

vulnerabilityAlerts.description: Security fixes bypass the weekly schedule; PR ordering is boosted by the isVulnerabilityAlert packageRule above.
